summary: A 1933 CCC-built L-4 cab, replaced in 1962 by an ODF cab on a 10-ft tower; staffed through 2017, found closed in 2023, on BLM land beside the PCT.

facts.design: ODF 14 x 14 ft flat-roof cab on a 10 ft wooden tower (1962); original 1933 L-4 cab on a 6 ft base
facts.status_note: Standing, but found closed up and unstaffed on a May 2023 visit

access.note: Cab closed up with a camera for remote monitoring as of May 2023; no source describes the cab as open to visitors. The site is BLM land inside the Cascade-Siskiyou National Monument, reached on foot from the Pacific Crest Trail.

visit.trail_note: From the Hobart Bluff trailhead, about a mile south on the Pacific Crest Trail, then a cutoff and a rough dirt road just under a mile to the summit (2017 visit account).

events.note: First lookout: an L-4 cab on a 6 ft base, completed by a CCC crew
Ira Tungate acted as lookout in the summer before a January 1935 notice; earliest named lookout in these sources
Thelma Sims stationed on the summit; a 1955 account counts her sixth or seventh year on the mountain
Lightning struck the lookout station in August; the only damage reported was to the telephone system
ODF replaced the 1933 cab with the present 14 x 14 ft flat-roof cab on a 10 ft tower; 1961 cabin raise and 1962 new tower per the Forest Lookouts history
A communications site was built on the summit and the lookout was electrified
Cellular One installed a tower and equipment building beside the cab; the view from the lookout was blocked
Cab raised four feet, which the history gives as a 9 ft 10 in tower with a new stair configuration
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register June 15, 2000
Staffed every summer through 2017; a July 2, 2017 visit found it staffed
Found closed up with a remote-monitoring camera on a May 2023 visit; BLM said it was no longer staffed. The closure date is not given in the sources

corrections.proposed: ODF 14 x 14 ft flat-roof cab on a 10 ft wooden tower (1962); original 1933 L-4 cab on a 6 ft base
corrections.why: L-4 describes only the 1933 original cab, which the ODF replaced in 1962 with the present cab.
The first cab was built in 1933; 1962 was the replacement, not the first construction.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR entry says the lookout is still in active service. The May 2023 visit and the BLM contact report it closed and no longer staffed. The story follows the 2023 evidence and notes the disagreement.
NHLR and firelookout.com give a 10 ft tower. The Forest Lookouts history records a 1993 four-foot raise giving 9 ft 10 in. The story reports both figures rather than choosing one.
NHLR gives 6,049 ft (1,844 m), which matches the brief. firelookout.com and the 2017 visit account give 6,091 ft. Elevation is not stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: Current status rests on one 2023 blog visit and a BLM contact that the blogger reports; ODF did not reply to the blogger. The NHLR still says active service, and the brief's access 'unknown' is now recorded as closed on that basis. Elevation disagrees: NHLR 6,049 ft (1,844 m) matches the brief's 1843.7 m, while firelookout.com and the 2017 visit say 6,091 ft. Tower height disagrees (10 ft vs 9 ft 10 in after a 1993 raise). The closure date between 2017 and 2023 is unknown. No wildfire response, rental or Forest Service connection appears in these sources. An undated ODF Forest Log article on the Struck staffing was found but not used, because its date and quotes were not confirmed. No photos were added because no image URL with a licence was confirmed. Story is about 385 words.
